text: PUBLISHER PITCH  /  OCTOBER 2026

Pitch claim grounded in LoomRoom’s GameDesign.md: first-person dungeon crawler framed by a miniature table, Dungeon Master, and bedroom setting. The cover figure is a project character model and is used as a mood image, not presented as a screenshot.

name: wordmark
text: LOOMROOM

name: premise
text: A dungeon crawler staged as a miniature adventure.

name: detail
text: Fight through authored rooms, find stronger gear, and build a character over a multi-floor run.

name: callout heading
text: The framing device

name: callout body
text: The bedroom table and Dungeon Master give the descent a story-shaped context.

This is the central positioning claim. The room and table are project framing. The game design describes 90% of play in the dungeon; avoid presenting the bedroom layer as equally large. Image is a concept asset for the Dungeon Master, not a final in-game screenshot.

title: Every attack spends a defensive resource

text: LOOMROOM

text: SHIELD

name: magic label
text: FIREBALL

name: tradeoff
text: OR

name: combat choice
text: Left hand: shield or spell

name: weapon detail
text: Swords favor reliable handling. Maces trade speed for stagger and guard pressure.

name: magic detail
text: Fireball pressures enemies at range. Heal trades mana and time for recovery.

Weapons and shield images are authored project art, while Fireball is a texture from the project’s spell pack. GameDesign.md specifies one-handed swords and maces, shield or spell in left hand, stamina-driven attacks and blocks. This slide presents the intended systems; the current design scope and precise implementation should be confirmed against a playable build.

text: A rat gnaws through the crypt while the Dungeon Master watches the board.

The game design states that a small supporting tabletop and Dungeon Master layer occurs between runs while about 90% of gameplay is in the dungeon. The project has bedroom and boss-stage assets. Images are textured art assets, not assembled scene screenshots.

title: The full descent is a production target

name: scope tag
text: DESIGN TARGET

name: scope caveat
text: Docs describe the full run. The current Dungeon1 asset is configured for four floors across two stages, so the 20-floor plan still requires production.

name: progression detail
text: Biome changes enemy families, room themes and loot bands. Depth sets the available equipment band.

The game design’s intended full-run layout is six three-floor biome blocks plus a two-floor finale. The current Unity asset Assets/Game/Levels/Dungeon1/Dungeon1.asset has two stages of two floors each. This slide expressly distinguishes design target from the configured current game data.

No contact, build URL, budget, platform commitment or release date is asserted. Fill these from team-approved and verified inputs before external circulation.
